purpose: Enterprise-oriented pre-AI corpus candidates for BRE language and framework expansion. Use 2020-12-31 as the clean baseline and 2023-01-01 as the transition comparison point.
selection_criteria: Open-source GitHub repository verified with git ls-remote.
Repository existed before or around the 2020 baseline where possible.
Represents languages and framework surfaces common in large enterprise systems.
Includes platform/config ecosystems such as Kubernetes, Kafka, Helm, Terraform, build systems, and application framework configuration.

repos.why_benchmark: Canonical enterprise Java framework with auto-configuration, dependency injection, starters, Maven/Gradle builds, and application config conventions.
repos.starter_task: Target a web auto-configuration or actuator behavior and verify BRE pulls source, tests, build files, and application config boundaries.

repos.why_benchmark: Core Java enterprise framework; useful for dependency-injection and framework-convention context tests.
repos.starter_task: Target an MVC or bean lifecycle path and measure whether BRE includes framework wiring and focused tests.

repos.why_benchmark: Enterprise event-streaming platform; context depends on producers, consumers, brokers, protocol definitions, and properties files.
repos.starter_task: Target consumer group assignment or producer config behavior and verify BRE pulls protocol, config, tests, and build context.

repos.why_benchmark: Large Java distributed database with configuration and storage/query subsystems.
repos.starter_task: Target a config-driven storage/query behavior and check whether BRE includes YAML and subsystem ownership files.

repos.why_benchmark: Large Java search engine with plugins, cluster behavior, REST APIs, and config surfaces.
repos.starter_task: Target a REST action or cluster setting and verify BRE includes handler, setting, tests, and build context.

repos.why_benchmark: Enterprise identity/auth system where missing config and provider wiring is risky.
repos.starter_task: Target authentication flow behavior and verify BRE pulls provider, config, tests, and build files.

repos.why_benchmark: Core .NET runtime and libraries; useful for C#/MSBuild enterprise context.
repos.starter_task: Target a library behavior and verify BRE includes project files, tests, shared props, and implementation.

repos.why_benchmark: Canonical enterprise C# web framework with routing, middleware, dependency injection, and appsettings config.
repos.starter_task: Target middleware or routing behavior and check whether BRE includes startup/config/project boundaries.

repos.why_benchmark: Enterprise ORM with provider abstractions, tests, and project boundaries.
repos.starter_task: Target query translation behavior and verify BRE includes provider, tests, and project files.

repos.why_benchmark: Canonical Python web framework; enterprise context often lives in settings, URL routing, models, migrations, and tests.
repos.starter_task: Target auth or ORM behavior and verify BRE includes settings, models, migration/test context, and package metadata.

repos.why_benchmark: Enterprise workflow orchestrator with plugin/provider boundaries and heavy Python config surfaces.
repos.starter_task: Target scheduler/operator behavior and verify BRE includes provider, config, tests, and dependency metadata.

repos.why_benchmark: Enterprise automation codebase where YAML and plugin/module conventions matter as much as Python imports.
repos.starter_task: Target module/plugin behavior and verify BRE includes module docs, YAML examples, and tests.

repos.why_benchmark: Large C++ service proxy with generated APIs, config schemas, Bazel, and production networking concerns.
repos.starter_task: Target filter or xDS behavior and verify BRE includes protobuf, config schema, tests, and Bazel ownership.

repos.why_benchmark: Cross-language serialization system where .proto schemas are critical context.
repos.starter_task: Target parser/generator behavior and verify BRE includes .proto schemas, C++ implementation, and build files.

repos.why_benchmark: Enterprise RPC stack with C++ core, generated protocol surfaces, and many language bindings.
repos.starter_task: Target resolver/channel behavior and verify BRE includes core, tests, proto, and build files.

repos.why_benchmark: Large C++ analytical database with parser, storage, query, and config-heavy surfaces.
repos.starter_task: Target SQL function/query behavior and verify BRE includes parser, function, tests, and CMake context.

repos.why_benchmark: Kubernetes is an enterprise platform boundary: API types, controllers, manifests, and deployment semantics drive context.
repos.starter_task: Target controller/API behavior and verify BRE includes API types, controller code, tests, and manifests.

repos.why_benchmark: Helm is the Kubernetes packaging layer; charts and values are critical context for deployment changes.
repos.starter_task: Target chart rendering or values behavior and verify BRE includes templates, chart metadata, tests, and Go code.

repos.why_benchmark: Infrastructure-as-code engine where HCL config and provider/plugin boundaries are central.
repos.starter_task: Target plan/apply behavior and verify BRE includes HCL tests, provider boundary, and Go implementation.

repos.why_benchmark: Enterprise frontend framework with DI, compiler, templates, and TypeScript-heavy monorepo layout.
repos.starter_task: Target router/compiler behavior and verify BRE includes TS implementation, tests, tsconfig, and framework metadata.

repos.why_benchmark: Compiler-sized TypeScript corpus useful for true TS parser hardening.
repos.starter_task: Target checker or parser behavior and verify BRE includes compiler source, fixtures, and tsconfig.

repos.why_benchmark: Enterprise observability app with backend, frontend, provisioning, deployment, and plugin surfaces.
repos.starter_task: Target alerting or datasource behavior and verify BRE includes backend, frontend, provisioning config, and tests.
